facts.raw_span: A 27-year-old man
history of a 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck
treated six years earlier by wide local excision
no sentinel lymph node biopsy, no adjuvant therapy
presented with hemoptysis and dyspnea
Vital signs were within normal limits
Physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe
Endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
Molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation but otherwise were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET)
Positron emission tomography (PET)/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass
an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone

concepts.why: Molecular studies were consistent with Ewing sarcoma/PNET and a malignant small round blue cell tumor was found in the lung lesion
The hyoid lesion was suspected to be a synchronous primary bone tumor, such as chondrosarcoma
The hyoid lesion was suspected to be a synchronous primary bone tumor, such as plasmacytoma
The hyoid lesion was suspected to be a synchronous primary bone tumor, such as osteosarcoma
The patient has a history of melanoma, which could have metastasized to the lung
A mass was found in the right lower lobe of the lung, which could be a primary lung cancer
The lung mass could be a metastasis from the Ewing sarcoma or another primary tumor
The patient has a malignant tumor, which could be a sarcoma

rationales.F02: History of melanoma increases the likelihood of metastatic melanoma.
rationales.F08: A mass in the right lower lobe is consistent with lung cancer or pulmonary metastasis.
rationales.F09: Malignant small round blue cell tumor is consistent with Ewing sarcoma or other sarcomas.
rationales.F10: Molecular studies consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) strongly support Ewing sarcoma.
rationales.F11: FDG-avid right lower lobe mass is consistent with lung cancer or pulmonary metastasis.
rationales.F12: Expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone is consistent with primary bone tumors such as chondrosarcoma, plasmacytoma, or osteosarcoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient has a history of melanoma and presents with a malignant small round blue cell tumor in the lung, which is consistent with a pulmonary metastasis. The molecular studies also support Ewing sarcoma, but the presence of a primary tumor in the hyoid bone and the patient's history of melanoma make pulmonary metastasis a more likely explanation for the lung lesion.
